question: During her recent visit to Iceland, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen held a joint press conference with Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir in Reykjavík, where an Icelandic journalist challenged her over reports that all questions had to be submitted in writing a day in advance1. The journalist ended with the pointed remark ‘are you unable to answer unscripted questions?

’ The President, momentarily taken aback, replied ‘the last part of your question is not known to me’, implying that she was unaware of any such demand. This exchange has since raised questions about transparency, press freedom and the President’s communication practices. In this context, can the Commission state: 1.

On how many occasions since the beginning of President von der Leyen’s mandate in 2019, and in which locations, have Commission staff or representatives of the President required journalists to submit questions in advance of a press conference?
Was the reported demand in Reykjavík initiated by Commission staff or by the Icelandic authorities, and what written record exists of this request?

What concrete measures will the Commission adopt to ensure that journalists are always able to ask unscripted questions in press events involving the President, and will the Commission commit to publishing clear rules of engagement for all such events?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.10.2025) The Commission attaches utmost importance to press freedom and transparency and actively promotes them through its policies and actions. It believes that a free and independent press is vital for fostering informed public debate.

To this end, the Commission strives to maintain the highest standards of transparency, accessibility, and openness in its interactions with the media and the public, providing timely and accurate information to facilitate informed reporting and public scrutiny.

These principles underpin all press events with the participation of the President of the Commission, where journalists are free to ask any questions they consider relevant. Before press conferences abroad involving the President of the Commission, the press team seeks to identify in advance key issues of interest to the local media. To this end, press officers liaise with their national counterparts.

In preparation for the press conference of the President of the Commission and Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir in Reykjavík, the Commission’s press team reached out to the press office of the Icelandic Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The exchange focused on practical aspects of the event organisation such as expected media attendance and the main topical issues for the Icelandic press.
